transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-12-30 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52m | Attendees: Priya, Ethan, Marco, Sara - Winterbridge: Lena, Marcus, Anya, Tom, Ivy

Summary (auto): Kickoff to align on network/access, deployment mode options (hosted/dedicated/private), security documentation (SOC2/KMS), pilot scope and next steps. Agreement to run a private deployment POC with limited traffic and a staging canary.

00:00 Priya Rao: Hi everyone thanks for making time today, happy holidays, I'll kick us off. Quick round robin intro?
00:08 Lena Ortiz: Hey I'm Lena VP Eng at Winterbridge, responsible for platform services, we'll be owning the integration.
00:13 Marcus Hale: Marcus, DevOps, I'll do the cloud infra and networking.
00:17 Anya Chen: Anya product, I'll own success metrics and verification.
00:20 Tom Brooks: Tom, security — primarily compliance and KMS key management questions.
00:24 Ivy Park: Ivy, SRE focusing on runbooks and alerting.
00:26 Priya Rao: Great, Redwood team — Ethan SE for technical deep dives, Marco will help on onboarding infra, Sara on adoption metrics.

02:00 Priya Rao: Goal for this call is to capture access needs, decide initial deployment mode for pilot, agree success criteria and action items. We typically see two common pilot shapes — hosted quickstart or private/VPC pilot when security is strict. Where are you leaning, Lena?
02:18 Lena Ortiz: We can't do sensitive customer data on third-party hosted endpoints initially, so leaning private. But we want to keep some non-sensitive workloads on hosted to save cost. So a mixed approach maybe.
02:35 Tom Brooks: To be clear, our blocker is encryption at rest under our KMS and audit logs we must retain on prem for six months. Also SSO and RBAC integration.
02:47 Ethan Cole: Absolutely, Redwood Private supports customer KMS and audit export, and Console has token-level tracing but we can route logs to your syslog or S3. Small note, sometimes our docs say "Redwood Private" but transcription here might show "Redwood Privet" in exports, ignore that.
03:10 Marcus Hale: How does peering work? We use transitive peering through our VPCs and have strict egress rules.
03:18 Marco Diaz: For VPC, we usually ask for a dedicated subnet and a peering conn. We'll provide a network diagram template. We support both VPC peering and private link depending on region and cloud. For transit gateways we have a playbook but it gets a bit detail-y.
03:45 Marcus Hale: Any specific firewall ports?
03:48 Marco Diaz: Yes 443 outbound to the control plane, and for inference nodes we need the internal port range for health checks - we'll send the exact list. Some customers also require NAT for egress.
04:05 Ivy Park: What about KV cache persistence? We want to ensure no KV written to external stores unless we enable it.
04:12 Ethan Cole: KV cache is in-memory on the serving nodes by default, not persisted unless you configure a cache-backend. We'll make sure that stays in-memory for your pilot.

06:10 Anya Chen: Success criteria from product side: sub‑second 90th latency under test load for chat flows, and embedding throughput of at least 1k QPS for async batch jobs. Also accuracy regressions <= 2% compared to our baseline.
06:28 Sara Kim: We'll help instrument those metrics via Console dashboards, and provide eval hooks to catch regressions.

08:00 Tom Brooks: Compliance — SOC2 reports and encryption key controls, do you have a bring-your-own key (BYOK) flow?
08:08 Priya Rao: Yes BYOK is supported on Redwood Private; we'll share the KMS integration docs. For hosted we have limited BYOK, but enterprise contracts can include stronger controls.
08:25 Tom Brooks: Also need audit log retention policy and log shipping.
08:29 Marco Diaz: Audit logs can be shipped to your S3 or SIEM. We'll include retention and sample log formats.

10:00 Lena Ortiz: Timeline — we're aiming to start a two‑week pilot early Jan and go to a production ramp in Q1 if pilot succeeds. Is that realistic for Redwood?
10:12 Priya Rao: Yes, that's typical. We'll prioritize the VPC intake template and a canary plan. Suggest a deep dive on week of Jan 6 to lock networking.

12:30 Marcus Hale: Bandwidth and instance sizing — how do you recommend sizing for our initial model? We expect bursts of short chat sessions and nightly batch embedding jobs.
12:45 Ethan Cole: For mixes like that we recommend a small serving pool with autoscale for chat and separate batch workers. We'll give recommended GPU types and quantization options. If you want cost swing, Redwood Optimize can recommend quant profiles per workload.
13:05 Marcus Hale: Do you have any prebuilt Terraform modules for provisioning the peering / endpoints?
13:12 Marco Diaz: We have a repo with Terraform examples; it's not fully turnkey for every cloud but it's a good starting point. We'll link that repo.

16:00 Anya Chen: Questions about model versions — we want to pin an eval set and ensure rollouts are gated. How does rollouts and A/B work?
16:10 Ethan Cole: Console supports canary rollout, traffic split, and automatic fallback. You can pin by model artifact hash. We'll set up a basic rollout policy in the pilot. Note that model quantization can alter outputs slightly so we'll align eval thresholds.

18:50 Tom Brooks: Data residency — some user data must never leave region. Can you ensure inference nodes are regionalized?
18:57 Marco Diaz: Yes you can pin clusters to regions. For Private deployments you control the VPC so that's enforced. For Hosted, we can route to region-specific endpoints but that's not air-gapped.

21:30 Lena Ortiz: Ok let's surface risks: networking complexity, audit log export, and SSO + RBAC mapping. Also cost if we run everything private.
21:45 Priya Rao: Agreed. We'll build a shoulder-to-shoulder plan: 1) network intake 2) SSO test account 3) staging canary 4) run throughput/latency tests.

24:00 Marcus Hale: One more — how do we handle secrets? Our ops policy forbids static tokens in code.
24:06 Ethan Cole: We can integrate with your KMS, and Console supports short-lived tokens via your IdP with SCIM provisioning. We'll send the SCIM/SAML guide.

27:40 Anya Chen: For the pilot, who will be our Redwood contacts and SLA for response?
27:46 Priya Rao: Primary contact me for project, Ethan for technical, Marco for infra. SLA for pilot triage is 4 business hours for P1 during business hours. We'll document escalation path.

30:05 Tom Brooks: About encryption in transit — are mutual TLS options available between our services and the inference pods?
30:12 Marco Diaz: We support mTLS for internal traffic via sidecar in Private installs; for hosted we use standard TLS. We'll include the mTLS steps in the runbook.

33:00 Sara Kim: We'll set up initial dashboards: latency p90/p99, token cost per request, embedding throughput, error rate and prompt eval regression. Share a sample query set and we'll configure alerts.

36:10 Priya Rao: Next steps recap — we'll send network diagram template, SOC2 + KMS docs, Terraform samples, and a proposed pilot runbook. You'll share VPC details and a list of SSO test accounts.

40:00 Marcus Hale: Sounds good. One nit — we've experimented with on-prem quantized models, curious if Redwood supports INT4/INT8 quant for speed/cost tradeoffs.
40:09 Ethan Cole: Yes we do, we can run quantized variants, but for the pilot we'll recommend a conservative INT8 profile and compare quality. Redwood Optimize can automate some of these recommendations.

44:30 Anya Chen: For evaluation — we'll provide a baseline set of prompts and expected outputs. Can Console surface regressions per prompt?
44:38 Sara Kim: Yes, we can attach evals to routes and fire alerts on regression. We'll show a demo in the technical deep dive.

47:55 Priya Rao: Any other questions?
48:02 Ivy Park: Quick ask — retention of telemetry, we need 90 days at min for metric retention.
48:08 Marco Diaz: That's fine, Console retention is configurable for enterprise tiers; we'll include retention SLAs in the doc.

50:00 Priya Rao: Great thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the packet later today. Appreciate the clarity on timeline — aiming for Jan pilot kickoff.
50:08 Lena Ortiz: Thanks all, look forward to the deep dive.
50:12 Tom Brooks: Thanks.

Auto-generated action items (repeat): Priya to send onboarding packet and runbook; Marcus to share VPC/CIDR; Ethan to provision demo tenant; Tom to share compliance list.

End of transcript.
